intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 (HMND14), a lower motor neuron disease, is caused by mutation in the gene encoding the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin (DCTN1) on chromosome 2p13.

paragraphs.text: In a lower motor neuron disease mapped to chromosome 2p13, Puls et al. (2003) screened a gene in the linked interval that encodes the largest subunit of dynactin (DCTN1). They found a single base-pair change that led to an amino acid substitution. This substitution was predicted to distort the folding of dynactin's microtubule-binding domain. In binding assays, the mutant protein bound less to microtubules.

agent.process_note: I read both papers, but only abstracts were available. Puls et al. (2003) reports linkage to 2p13 (4 Mb), a single base-pair missense change in the gene for the largest dynactin subunit, and reduced microtubule binding. The abstract does not name the variant, its zygosity, the family (size, ancestry), the clinical details (such as vocal cord paralysis) or the inheritance pattern. As a result, I wrote no allelic variant and no clinical features or inheritance section. The symbol DCTN1 is not in the Puls abstract. I took it from Münch et al. (2004), which names the p150 subunit of dynactin as DCTN1. The AD inheritance in relationships comes from the entry title, not from the abstracts. Münch et al. (2004) is about DCTN1 variants in ALS (T1249I, M571T, R785W), not this disorder, so I did not cite it. No HGNC MIM number or reference data were supplied for the gene.
